meta.title: Wing Fighter Strategy Guide
meta.tagline: Build smarter. Counter stronger opponents. Spend where it matters.
meta.metaLine: Updated Oct 18, 2026 · mechanics and strategy validation
meta.author: ashpool

content.title: Start Here: What Every Player Should Know

content.html: Battle Power (BP) measures investment, but it doesn’t tell you whether your build is good for the fight. A lower-BP player can win with better stat choices and the right counter.
This guide covers the builds, mechanics, and spending decisions that matter in PVP and PVE. Five principles will help you use the details that follow.
A well-built 30M player can beat a poorly built 45M player. Before judging a matchup by BP, look at the opponent’s stats, formation, and likely weaknesses.

content.title: 2. Your build works as a whole

content.html: Chip formations set your strategy. Drones, sentinels, mech spirits, and engines support it. Pilots provide the foundation, while Camp Tech and equipment add strength. Invest in combinations that help each other, not just the upgrades that add the most BP.
Crit is strongest when opponents lack Crit Resistance. Dodge works against low Hit Rate. Burn punishes Dodge, but Burn Decrease limits its damage. Use the formation that exploits the matchup.

Defense Break and Defense affect damage across your entire build. Falling behind on pilots creates a disadvantage that is difficult to overcome with equipment alone. Keep both Physical Defense and Energy Defense competitive.

Resources are limited. Start with a reliable PVE boss setup and one PVP build you actually use. Max accessible drones and sentinels before chasing rare upgrades, and spend to fix the weakness that is costing you fights.
Choose the section that matches your goal. You don’t need to read everything in order.

cells: Understand why stronger players sometimes lose
Figure out where to invest next
Burn Drones and PVE Burn Build
Sentinel Investment Path and Mech Investment Strategy

content.html: Understand counters, choose complementary stats, and learn what to fix when a build loses.
You can’t optimize every possible formation. Specialize in the matchups that matter most to you.

There is no formation that beats everything. Dodge struggles against high Hit Rate; Crit struggles against Crit Resistance; Burn has to overcome Burn Decrease. Pick your formation for the opponent rather than trying to cover every weakness at once.

content.title: Find What's Holding Your Build Back

content.html: When you lose, identify the problem before spending more resources:

items.html: Attacks miss: increase Hit Rate or switch to Burn against a Dodge-heavy opponent.
Critical hits kill you: add Crit Resistance to make crits less likely. If the crits that land hit too hard, add Crit Damage Reduction.
Damage builds too slowly: improve survivability or choose a faster damage source.
Your hits are weak: check Defense Break against the opponent’s Defense.
Burn wears you down: equip Burn Decrease; Dodge cannot stop burn ticks already applied.

content.html: Upgrade the weakness that is losing you fights, not simply the stat that raises BP the most.
Your primary attribute determines how you fight. Your secondary attributes determine which opponents you can handle.

items.html: Dodge + Crit Resistance: avoid direct hits and reduce the chance that hits become crits; healing helps in longer fights.
Dodge + Hit Rate: survive against other Dodge builds while landing more of your own attacks.
Crit + Hit Rate: land powerful attacks through Dodge.
Crit + Crit Resistance: trade some offensive coverage for protection in crit matchups.
Burn + Crit Resistance: keep burn damage ticking while surviving counterattacks.

content.html: These are useful pairings, not hard rules. Committing to a few complementary stats usually works better than spreading chips across unrelated bonuses.

BP reflects raw progression, not how efficiently a player fights. Keep pilot investment outpacing BP inflation instead of chasing BP for its own sake. In Star Scramble, matchmaking is based on total legion BP, so inefficient upgrades affect the team. Planet Wars and Military Drills reward raw strength more directly. Hyper Battlefield placement depends on BP and prior results, but the formula is undisclosed: BF5 is easiest, BF1 hardest, and moving from BF2 to BF1 can be a major difficulty jump.

For some players, pausing gear evolution around one-star rainbow or stopping sentinel leveling at 80 keeps a leaner build; others prefer the raw power from further upgrades. Camp Tech and mech passives can add unavoidable BP. Prioritize useful combat gains over artificial BP suppression.

Free-to-play players can’t fully develop every setup at once. Focus on a PVE boss build and one dependable PVP formation before diversifying. Rare sentinels, advanced mechs, and recast materials are long-term investments; spreading them across unfinished projects delays results.

content.title: Part 2: Building for PVE and PVP

content.html: Start with the build that matches your goal. These are recommended setups, not guarantees: swap components when the opponent calls for it. Part 3 covers the underlying mechanics.

A good starting point is Crit + Hit Rate for PVP offense, Dodge + Crit Resistance for PVP defense, and Burn + Crit for PVE. Once you can reach 100% Burn Enhancement without burn chips, you may free the third formation for PVP Burn + Crit Resistance—provided your boss damage stays competitive without the dedicated PVE chips. See Choosing Your Three Formations for when to switch.

For bosses, reach 100% effective Burn Enhancement first. Then strengthen the damage your burning drones deal through Crit Rate, Crit Damage, and the Evil Eye / Star Envoy combination. Because Evil Eye's conversion improves as it levels, judge the value of additional crit by your actual damage, not by an assumed burn-crit cap.

cells: Core damage dealers. Star Envoy requires three burn drones to activate.
Burn / Crit while you need Burn chips; consider shared Crit / Hit Rate after 100% burn without chips
Sharing Crit / Hit Rate with PVP saves a formation, but may cost PVE damage versus a dedicated PVE-focused chip setup; compare boss results. See Choosing Your Three Formations.
Flashstrike (N-class), developed with relevant Crit Damage / Sentinel Enhancement passives; Savageplate or Gridstar can be alternatives.
Flashstrike’s temporary damage-boost effect can also benefit drones. The multi-passive Flashstrike recipe is a legion recommendation; compare your actual available slots and boss results.
Star Envoy + Evil Eye + (Dragon Emperor or Berserk Dragon)
Star Envoy and Evil Eye are the core pair; use Magic Armor as the third when you need more Burn Enhancement.

content.html: Win through survivability. Dodge avoids many direct hits, Crit Resistance makes enemy crits less likely, and healing extends the fight. Crit Damage Reduction is the stat that makes a crit smaller when it does land.

cells: Dodge direct hits, then reduce the chance that landed hits crit. Crit Damage Reduction reduces the size of any crits that still land.
At a fully developed gold Heal Enhancement passive (level 10), the bonus is +100 percentage points. A fully evolved sentinel develops its passive slots to level 10.
Sagittarius (burner for long fights); Apus is an accessible early alternative
Burn damage compounds over the long fights this build creates. Apus still works at lower BP, but tops out faster.
Burn Decrease vs. a burner, Crit Resistance otherwise

Burn Decrease is the one defensive gap this build can't close through dodge or heal. Against non-burners, Crit Resistance reduces the chance of big crit spikes; it does not reduce damage from crits that still land.

content.html: In long fights, a maxed Gridstar with gold Heal Enhancement, Ladybug, Berserk Dragon, and Aqua Spirit can restore substantial HP while reducing incoming damage. Actual healing depends on the matchup and investment.

For matchups where your opponent has low Crit Resistance. Pair with enough Hit Rate to land attacks against high-Dodge opponents. Crit rate in PVP is capped at 80% net of opponent crit resistance, so raw crit above 80% is still useful against opponents running significant crit resistance.

cells: Stormquill or SavagePlate with gold crit damage + crit rate
Stormquill reduces enemy damage boost; it is a defensive-debuff option, not an inherently crit-focused skill. Savageplate’s fast direct attack is more offense-oriented.
Use the Conqueror fighter with its matching Titan gear to qualify for the applicable set bonus; the fighter alone is not a 5-piece set.
Flame Stinger + Venom Scorpion + Battle Diva (or Gloom Moon when opponent dodge is high)
Crit-damage amplifier + finisher + crit-denial, swap Battle Diva for Gloom Moon vs high-dodge targets
Stack with Gloom Moon if swapped in

content.html: Preference: Burn + Crit Resistance is my recommended dedicated PVP burn formation. Burn can pressure high-Dodge opponents, while Crit Resistance lowers the chance of enemy crits.
Its main weakness is strong healing that can outlast burn ticks. Against those opponents, switch to a sentinel with Heal Reduction.

cells: 3 burn drones (e.g., 2x Ninja + Sagittarius, or Lich + Sagi + Lyra at scale)
Star Envoy’s three-burn-drone condition is a reason to plan the drone trio together.
Build raw Burn Enhancement to offset the opponent’s Burn Decrease; effective Burn Enhancement is capped at 100%.
Arcglow (sustain), or Glimshade when you can keep the target burning; aim for useful Healing / Sentinel Enhancement passives
Burn needs long fights to compound; a sustain sentinel keeps you in the fight long enough.

Different from the PVE build: Aqua Spirit's emergency damage reduction and Ladybug's healing floor matter more in PVP, and Evil Eye's crit conversion is less relevant when you don't have the room to stack crit past the cap.
Burn skills and ticks already pressure Dodge. Choose Hit Rate only when landing more direct attacks matters in that matchup.

content.html: If your PVE damage still relies on Burn chips, do not move those chips merely to complete this PVP formation. First test that your boss damage remains competitive without them. The third saved formation is a tradeoff between dedicated PVE performance and more PVP options.

cells: Consider burning-drone skills and ongoing burn against high Dodge. If you keep Crit, add Hit Rate and consider Gloom Moon.
Use Crit Resistance and consider Battle Diva.
Equip Flame Stinger for 25% dmg boost below 35% HP
Use a sentinel with Heal Reduction, such as SavagePlate or Rendclaw.
Switch to the Burn Decrease engine. See Countering Burn in PVP.
Watch for Burn. Dodge and healing do not prevent burn ticks already applied.
Default to Dodge / Crit Resistance (Formation 2) with the Crit Resistance engine. Switch to the Burn Decrease engine against burn-heavy opponents.

content.html: This is the technical reference behind the recommended builds: pilots, chips, drones, sentinels, mechs, engines, Camp Tech, and equipment. Jump to the system you want to improve.

Pilots improve Physical and Energy Defense Break (PDB, EDB) and Physical and Energy Defense (PD, ED). These stats affect damage dealt and received across your build. Neglect them and you may lose badly to players with similar BP.

cells: Offensive, your physical attacks vs. opponent's PD
Offensive, your energy attacks vs. opponent's ED
Defensive, opponent's physical attacks vs. your PD
Defensive, opponent's energy attacks vs. your ED

content.title: Why Pilots Matter More Than They Look

items.html: You need to be close enough on these stats to compete. If your offense (PDB/EDB) and defense (PD/ED) are roughly comparable to opponents at your BP, you can win by exploiting an advantage in chips, drones, sentinels, mechs, or passives. If your pilots lag, you're hunting for a much bigger exploitable gap elsewhere, and against a well-built opponent that gap may not exist.
Pilots compound with everything else, so a player with mediocre gear but well-developed pilots is unusually tough for their BP. Starting fresh, I'd put pilots first.

content.html: Exactly one pilot can be equipped, and switching it is free except that the full Star Scramble defensive build is locked during the event. Every pilot still contributes its passive stat values while unequipped; equipping one increases that pilot’s Defense and Defense Break contribution to approximately 4× its unequipped amount. Passive skill bonuses do not get a 4× multiplier.
Example: six-star SR Lancelot provides +80 EDB and +80 PD when unequipped, or +320 of each when equipped. Awakened, the example rises to +100 each unequipped or +400 each equipped.

Pick the first awakening based on the opponents you actually face. A physical player facing energy opponents more often may awaken Hestia before Freya. If you use both damage types, all four combinations are useful. Change equipped pilots between Star Scramble attacks; your defensive pilot is fixed once defense is submitted.

Most common pilot mistake: a physical-damage player maxes PDB and PD and lets EDB and ED lag. You don't get to pick what your opponent throws at you, and an energy build will tear through a defender who ignored ED. Max both PD and ED regardless of your offensive specialization.
Offense is more defensible to specialize, since you're choosing your own build, but maxing both PDB and EDB is still the long-term goal, some PVE encounters and PVP matchups reward the flexibility.

content.title: Pilot Evolution, Awakening, and Extra Shards

content.html: Unlock pilots broadly and complete the first two Pilot Badge evolutions, which have the same Badge requirements across rarities. Later evolutions require growing numbers of pilot-specific shards and, at high stars, additional rarity-based shards. Pilot-specific drops are often random; SR selectables are available in the Pilot Event, Hyper Battlefield shop, and some other sources.

A pilot reaches full regular evolution at six stars. Shards of that pilot acquired afterward become automatically usable extra shards of its rarity, with no manual conversion. When deciding which N or R pilot to finish next, weigh its immediate stat increase, required cost, and how many waiting shards will unlock.

Awaken the two SR pilots you actually equip for one damage type, or up to four if you routinely play both physical and energy. Then work on getting your N and R roster to six stars. After that, choose between accessible R awakenings for broad stats and stronger but much more expensive SR awakenings for their specific passive bonuses; there is no fixed universal order. SSR awakening is an exceptionally long-term goal because SSR shards are concentrated in special events.

These costs use extra/generic shards, not more shards of the pilot being awakened. Additional Pilot Badges are also required. Example screenshots showed 1,800 Pilot Badges for an SR awakening, plus the three shard requirements above. Both evolved and awakened unequipped pilots continue contributing their Defense/Defense Break and passive bonuses.

content.title: Pilot Training: Valuable Passives, Lean BP

content.html: Training Guides raise a pilot’s passive skill from level 1 through level 10. Training increases the passive and BP, not Defense or Defense Break. Each level gives the same increment to the passive but successive levels cost more Training Guides. The training cost schedule is identical for N, R, SR, and SSR.

Train several valuable SR and SSR PvP passives to moderate levels before pushing individual passives to level 10. Higher-rarity pilots generally have better passives for the same Training Guide costs. Some N and R passives primarily help PVE; leaving those untrained avoids BP growth that does little for PvP matchmaking. Do not skip a useful PvP passive merely to suppress BP.

Do not use fixed Defense / Defense Break targets per million BP. Older targets have become unreliable as the game added BP-inflating systems. Continuously prioritize pilots and compare actual opponents: raise PDB only for physical damage, EDB only for energy damage, and improve both PD and ED regardless of gear type. For players using physical and energy builds, all four stats matter.
Use opponent attribute comparison to identify the gap that is losing fights. Pilots are a continuing priority, not an upgrade you complete once you hit a numerical BP benchmark.

content.title: Defense Break vs. Defense: How the Math Works

content.html: Defense Break (your offensive stat) is compared against the opponent's Defense (their defensive stat). The difference between the two, not the raw values, drives a damage multiplier on top of everything else you've built. The same math applies in reverse on incoming damage: opponent's PDB vs. your PD, and opponent's EDB vs. your ED.
If your Break ≥ enemy Defense (neutral or bonus zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 + ((Your Break − Enemy Defense) / 1000)
If your Break < enemy Defense (penalty zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 / (1 + ((Enemy Defense − Your Break) / 1000))

The only thing that matters is the gap: Your Break minus Enemy Defense. That gap places you in one of three zones: below (penalty), equal (neutral, 1.00x), or above (bonus). The same logic applies on the defensive side: when your PD exceeds an opponent's PDB, they are in their penalty zone against you.

When your Defense Break matches the enemy’s Defense, the multiplier is 1.00×: neither a penalty nor a bonus. There is no sudden damage cliff or jump at parity. The multiplier changes smoothly as the gap closes. Getting near parity is valuable, but Defense Break above parity can still help; compare it with the value of your other upgrades.
A positive Break gap increases damage, while a negative gap reduces it. The effects are reciprocal rather than mirror-image percentage changes:

cells: Closing a deficit improves every hit.
At −500, damage is about two-thirds of normal.

content.html: Priority: close a major Break deficit first. Parity is a useful reference, not a point where returns abruptly change; compare further Defense Break with other upgrades before spending.

Chip Formations let you save three specialized sets of stat chips and choose the one that suits the fight. Your chip strategy determines whether you focus on dealing damage, avoiding attacks, or outlasting an opponent. Sentinels, mechs, engines, and drones should support that choice.

Each chip set is tied to one of your underlying battle formations and needs to align with that formation's other equipment (gems, gears, drones, sentinels). Most players dedicate one formation to PVE and the other two to PVP.

You have three complete saved formations. Switching slots changes gear, pilots, drones, sentinels, and mechs together without manually re-equipping individual pieces. Most players start with a dedicated PVE formation and one primary PVP formation, then use the third slot for flexibility.

cells: PVE Burn evolving toward Crit chips
First dedicated PVE setup; keep effective Burn Enhancement at 100%
Crit / Hit or Dodge / Crit Resistance
Burn / Crit Resistance, another counter, or an alternate PVE setup

content.html: For an advanced PVE build, gradually replace Burn chips with Crit Rate chips only while keeping 100% effective Burn Enhancement. For example, 90% native Burn Enhancement plus a blue sentinel passive supplying 15% gives 105% raw (100% effective), allowing no Burn chips at all. This Crit-chip PVE setup can also support PVP, but swap PVE-specific drones and Mech Spirits, including Evil Eye, before PVP.

cells: Entire defensive build is locked for the whole event
Change the full build or equipped pilot before each attack
Defense uses the exact formation currently equipped at the moment you are attacked

content.html: Warning: after using a PVE formation, switch back to your intended PVP defense. In Planet Wars and Military Drills you can be attacked while still wearing your boss setup.

content.title: Dodge vs. Crit: When to Switch

content.html: Pick the offensive or defensive emphasis that your opponent counters least. High enemy Dodge favors more Hit Rate or burn-drone skills; high enemy Crit Rate makes Crit Resistance useful on defense. Going above a cap can still matter when the opponent applies a counter, but check the effective stat rather than raw numbers alone.

items.html: Opponent has low Crit Resistance? Favor Crit, their defense can't deny what you're throwing.
Opponent has low Hit Rate? Favor Dodge, net dodge stays high, so your chips do real work.

Opponent has high Dodge and high Hit Rate? Burn is often a useful attack choice: burning-drone skills bypass the normal Hit-versus-Dodge check and existing burn ticks continue even if later normal attacks miss. Their high Hit Rate also makes a Dodge-only defense less reliable. Drone normal attacks can still miss.

content.html: Separate from the primary pick: make sure your Hit Rate is high enough to land attacks against high-Dodge opponents. Hit Rate is a prerequisite for crit, not a substitute for the primary.
Most important caps apply after your opponent's counters. Going above a cap isn't necessarily wasted in PVP.

cells: Effective after opponent Burn Decrease. PVE bosses generally have none; PVP may require more than 100% raw to reach the cap.
Your dodge minus opponent's hit rate; raw dodge can exceed 80%.
Your crit rate minus opponent's crit resistance; raw crit can exceed 80%.
80% effective for ordinary direct crits and for Burn Crit Rate; displayed Crit Rate may exceed 80%, which matters for Evil Eye conversion.

content.html: Hit, dodge, and crit don't apply to every attack. Knowing what's on and off the dice roll matters for passive priorities and for how you think about damage sources:

items.html: Hit and Dodge apply to: weapon and drone normal attacks. Weapon crit chance uses global and weapon-specific stats; drone normal attacks normally use Spot Weakness for crit chance.
Always hit, normally do not crit: drone skills, sentinel skills, and mech skills. Their damage does not depend on Hit Rate.
Evil Eye exception: equipped Evil Eye allows burning-drone normal attacks and skills to crit using its conversion of Crit Rate.

content.html: These differences matter when choosing passives. For example, Sentinel Enhancement improves sentinel skills that do not need a Hit Rate roll.

content.label: Hard cap
content.html: The burning-drone enhancement multiplier is capped at 2.0× (a maximum +100% effective enhancement), and floored at 1.0×. In the combat-mechanics model, the net bonus depends on your Burning Enhancement minus the enemy’s Burning Decrease. That means how much raw enhancement you need depends on the actual target:

items.html: PVE against a boss with no Burning Decrease: 100% raw Burning Enhancement reaches the 100% effective bonus cap. Beyond that, more enhancement adds nothing against that target. Do not assume every PVE enemy has identical defenses without checking.
PVP vs. opponent with no Burn Decrease: Same as PVE, 100% raw = 100% effective. Past 100% does nothing.
PVP vs. opponent with 50% Burn Decrease: Need 150% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Burn chips past 150% start to over-shoot.
PVP vs. opponent with 100% Burn Decrease: Need 200% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Still capped at 100% effective, just takes more raw to get there.

content.html: For a target with zero Burning Decrease, 100% raw Burning Enhancement reaches the cap. Against a player with Burning Decrease, up to 100% plus the opponent’s Burning Decrease can be useful. Importantly, the mechanics model floors the elemental multiplier at 1.0×: Burning Decrease can cancel an enhancement bonus, but does not reduce burning-drone damage below its unenhanced baseline through this multiplier alone.
For PVE, once chips, sentinel passives, mech bonuses, and Camp Tech reach the cap together, use remaining chip slots for Crit or other damage stats.

content.title: How Crit Works with Burn Drones

content.html: Ordinary direct-hit Crit Rate is effectively capped at 80% after subtracting the opponent’s Crit Resistance, but the displayed Crit Rate stat can be much higher. Burn Crit Rate also has an 80% effective cap. Evil Eye (SR Mech Spirit) converts eligible Crit Rate above the target’s Crit Resistance into Burn Crit Rate. The conversion uses the full eligible Crit Rate, including amounts above the ordinary 80% crit cap, until Burn Crit Rate itself reaches 80%.

At Evil Eye skill level 1, each 10% eligible Crit Rate produces about 2% Burn Crit Rate; at level 13 (Mech Level 60), each 10% produces 5.6% and the skill also grants +25.5% Burn Damage Boost at the start of battle. Against a PVE target assumed to have no Crit Resistance, max Evil Eye needs approximately 142.9% displayed Crit Rate to reach 80% Burn Crit Rate. PVE Crit Resistance is believed to be zero but has not been definitively verified.

cells: Max Evil Eye Burn Crit Rate

content.html: For PVE Burn, first achieve 100% effective Burn Enhancement, then reach 80% effective Burn Crit Rate, then keep increasing your relevant Defense Break. Additional Crit Rate beyond the PVE cap is still useful if you share this formation with a PVP Crit build, because PVP opponents may have significant Crit Resistance. Remove Evil Eye for PVP: legion battle experience indicates that its conversion eliminates the normal weapon crits required by Toad Lord; do not recommend the two together.

Burn pressures Dodge because burning-drone skills do not make an ordinary Hit-versus-Dodge roll, and applied burn stacks keep ticking even if later attacks miss. Burning-drone normal attacks can still be dodged. Burn generally becomes more dangerous as stacks and longer-fight buffs accumulate.

Start with Burning Decrease against a burn-heavy opponent. Choose the Burning Decrease engine, then consider additional decrease from other sources if your opponent still has a large net burn advantage. Dodge can avoid direct weapon and drone normal attacks, but it does not counter already-applied burn ticks or burning-drone skills. Keep Dodge only if it still helps against the opponent’s other damage.

Think in terms of which formation needs each chip, not a fixed number assigned to every stat. For a Crit / Hit Rate formation, seek chips with those complementary attributes; for Dodge / Crit Resistance, favor those two; and for your burn formation, prioritize Burn Enhancement until your non-chip sources reach the effective burn cap. If you later repurpose the burn formation for PVP, Crit Resistance becomes a useful secondary. Check the actual attributes and grade before replacing an existing chip.

content.title: Auto Mode Setup in the Chip Factory

content.html: The Chip Factory's Auto Mode can run chip manufacturing continuously and pause when a potentially useful chip appears. Configure its filters separately for each formation.

“Stop when chip rating increases” is the convenient option: it pauses on chips rated above the piece currently in that slot. In Ashpool’s legion explanation, leaving the minimum grade at the lowest setting avoids excluding potentially useful chips. The rating check can still miss a chip with stronger advanced attributes but lower overall rating, so review promising candidates before replacing anything.

items.html: Formation 1 (Crit / Hit): Crit Rate primary, Hit Rate secondary
Formation 2 (Dodge / Crit Resistance): Dodge Rate primary, Crit Resistance secondary

Formation 3: While building PVE, accept Burn Enhancement or Crit Rate as your main target. After switching to PVP Burn, prioritize Burn Enhancement with Crit Resistance. Use OR between alternative chip targets; use AND only when both attributes must appear on the same chip.

content.html: Check the Auto Mode filter preview before leaving production running. OR accepts either target; AND requires both together. A tighter attribute filter gives fewer candidates. For the most thorough search, turn off “Stop when chip rating increases,” keep a low minimum grade, and manually review the results; for less daily effort, leave the rating check on and accept that it may overlook some niche upgrades.

Do not automatically raise the minimum chip grade as your factory levels. Lower-grade chips can occasionally improve an advanced stat even when their total rating is lower. Keep a low grade floor if you are willing to review more results; raise it only to save time when your existing chips are already strong. This is a choice about how much manual screening you want, not a universal Iridium/Aether/Quantum cutoff.

Burn works well for boss damage and remains useful in PVP against Dodge-heavy opponents. Burning-drone skills and burn ticks do not use the ordinary Hit-versus-Dodge check, although drone normal attacks do. Burn also gains value as stacks and longer-fight bonuses accumulate. The main decisions are which three burn drones to use and which one to develop next.

Start by maxing 1-2 Ninjas. They're cheap to level, and a maxed Ninja can outperform an under-leveled higher-rarity drone (same star-scaling logic that makes maxed Gridstars beat low-star SSRs). Two maxed Ninjas give you a working burn build today.

cells: 1–2 maxed Ninjas + 1 unleveled R or SR
Ninjas carry the build while you progress your third drone
Accessible lineup that can remain useful while you add an SR later
2 maxed Ninjas + 1 maxed SR (Sagittarius / Lyra / Fornax)
Higher-ceiling option; only pursue when you can finish the SR
Multiple developed SRs, or a strong mixed R/SR trio
Choose by passive synergy and completed upgrades, not rarity alone

content.html: After Ninjas, choose one drone to finish next. You can mix R and SR drones in the same lineup; the decision here is where to spend scarce upgrade resources first.

items.html: R-tier: Faster to max, lower ceiling. A practical next project for F2P and lighter spenders. Options: Lich, Scorpion Lion, Cerberus.

SR-tier: Slower and more expensive, higher ceiling. SR burners (Sagittarius, Lyra, Fornax) outperform R drones once leveled. A practical next project once you can afford to develop one. Two maxed Ninjas plus one developed SR is useful; later, Lich + Sagittarius + Lyra or another mixed trio may be worth testing.

content.html: The mistake is spreading materials across several unfinished upgrades, not combining rarities. A developed R drone can belong alongside SR drones when its skill helps the whole team.

Preference: I favor Lich among accessible R-tier burn drones because its listed burn bonus appears broadly useful. The exact advantage over Cerberus and Scorpion Lion depends on your lineup and still needs battle-log testing. In particular, the combat-mechanics paper has not verified how Lich combines with Sagittarius and Star Envoy.

cells: Listed +15% burn-damage bonus; exact stacking with other burn buffs unverified

Likely valuable as a broad burn buff. The mechanics paper suggests Lich may add to the same Flaming bonus pool as Sagittarius and Star Envoy, but has not tested it. Do not assume it is a separate 1.15× multiplier on every tick.
Skill damage 255% + 3.5% per burn stack (max ~276% at 6 stacks)
Narrower benefit: about +8% to Cerberus's own listed skill multiplier at six stacks (276% vs. 255%), before interactions with other effects. Its value relative to Lich still needs testing.
+1 burn stack when recoil is active

Situational. Burn has a six-stack FIFO limit, so an extra stack can replace an older one rather than increase the stack count. Its value depends on recoil being active and on which stack is displaced. Test it against your actual lineup.

content.html: A good rule of thumb is to prefer bonuses that help the whole burn setup consistently over effects that need special conditions. Lich looks promising on that basis, but the exact ranking is a recommendation, not verified damage math.

content.title: Drones and Crit: What Actually Converts

content.html: Without Evil Eye, drone normal attacks do not use global Crit Rate. They need the Spot Weakness passive to crit, and Raging Assault increases the damage of those crits. Spot Weakness still has value by itself; Raging Assault without a way to crit does not.

items.html: With Evil Eye: burning-drone normal attacks and skills can crit using Evil Eye’s converted Crit Rate and the global Crit Damage multiplier. These replace the ordinary Spot Weakness / Raging Assault interaction for those attacks.
Burn ticks: the damage-over-time effect does not itself crit; it uses its own burn damage mechanics.

content.html: A fully developed drone has five passive slots, each reaching level 7 after 35 passive upgrades. Full evolution requires 48 copies total (the original and 47 others), because higher tiers need multiple duplicates. Drones of different rarities can be mixed within a formation.

Save or lock desirable gold and purple passive outcomes, rather than protecting a gold passive that does not help your build. Drone recasts are particularly efficient during Drone Events because Modified Chips count toward event milestones at 2× their number.

Drone transposition costs 300 diamonds. Both drones must be the same rarity, at least five stars, and have no unsaved recast result. Transposition exchanges all five passive types and colors between the two drones, while the passive levels stay on their original drones. This lets a low-evolution same-rarity donor hunt a rare passive before transferring it to a heavily evolved main drone.
Lich: its level-4 skill gives +15% Burn Damage for all drones throughout the battle; the exact stacking relationship with other damage bonuses has not been independently verified.
Build a roster of sentinels with different passive combinations so you can swap between them to exploit specific weaknesses in your opponent's build.

Sentinel rarities are N, R, G, SR, SSR (Flashstrike is N-class). Each sentinel has four passive slots regardless of rarity. Evolution to 40 stars uses 40 total copies, including the original, and can bring all four passives to level 10. Evolution also increases Attack and HP; the main strategic reason to finish it is maximizing passives. More evolution beyond 40 stars does not improve them.

All sentinel rarities share the same leveling system. Overclock Chips level the active skill, whose maximum is reached at sentinel level 80. Further leveling up to 150 increases raw stats and BP at a sharply rising chip cost without improving the active skill. Stopping at 80 favors BP efficiency; going higher can make sense when raw strength matters, such as Planet Wars or Military Drills. Resetting a sentinel recovers invested Overclock Chips.

Healing Enhancement applies across eligible healing sources, including Ladybug and Cheat Death. Sentinel Enhancement amplifies only sentinel healing/damage, not Ladybug or Cheat Death healing. At level 10, gold/purple/blue Healing Enhancement provide +100%/+80%/+60%, stacking additively with one another. Gold Sentinel Enhancement is +75% at maximum and is a separate multiplier for sentinel healing. Enemy Healing Reduction and Sentinel Reduction counter the corresponding bonuses.

content.title: Sentinel Passives: What the Odds Really Mean

content.html: Your fully developed sentinel may offer several passive slots, in gold, purple, or blue. The published per-slot rates below are useful for planning; confirm how many slots are actually available on the sentinel you are rerolling and remember that duplicate-family restrictions may change the effective chances.
Finding a gold passive isn't particularly rare. Finding the right gold passive is a different story.

content.title: How Many Recasts Might It Take?

content.html: The table assumes each available slot independently has a 0.5% chance of yielding one particular gold passive. That is an illustrative planning model, not a guarantee of the game’s duplicate-handling behavior. A recast rerolls the unlocked slots; locking one protects it but leaves fewer chances. Use your actual number of open slots rather than assuming every sentinel offers four.

The dollar estimates assume a flat 20 recast chips per recast and $3 per 20 chips. They exclude Protection Core costs and ignore free chips or free recasts, which can substantially reduce cash spending. Real costs can also differ if the game charges more when passives are locked. These averages are not guarantees; duplicate-passive restrictions and the game’s handling of unavailable outcomes are not fully documented.

Your legion reports that different colors of the same passive can coexist on a developed sentinel (for example, gold and purple Heal Enhancement). Do not plan on two copies of the same color and type. Because duplicate eligibility is not fully documented in the supplied mechanics paper, confirm the available combinations in-game before buying recast materials.

Preference: Prioritize one excellent gold passive on each sentinel before spending heavily to chase a second. A strong gold paired with useful purples is already an effective sentinel. Perfect rolls can take hundreds of attempts and the same resources could improve other parts of your build. A second gold is worth chasing only when its expected benefit outweighs that cost.
Get one gold passive that supports your build, then fill the other slots with useful supporting bonuses. A second ideal gold is a long-term upgrade, not a prerequisite.

cells: Crit damage, crit rate, sentinel enhancement
Other helpful damage or counter passives
Crit Damage Reduction, heal reduction, sentinel enhancement

content.html: Attack and HP passives add flat values, so they often contribute less to developed builds. Elemental Enhance/Decrease passives can be strong when they match your formation, but are less useful if you rarely run that element.
Role-specific passive targets by sentinel:

items.html: Gridstar (defensive): Prioritize Gold Heal Enhancement for sustain. Heal Reduction or Crit Damage Reduction can support other Gridstar variants. A separate anti-heal Gridstar with multiple Heal Reduction passives may work well against healing-dependent opponents, but check the net Healing Enhance–Decrease totals; it will not automatically shut off every healing source.

SavagePlate (offensive): Gold Crit Damage (primary); Gold Heal Reduce as the second gold to counter heal-stacked defenders. Sentinel Enhancement is also strong here because its 2-second cycle fires often.

Arcglow (SR, sustain pick): Gold Heal Enhance, Purple Heal Enhance, Blue Heal Enhance, Gold Sentinel Enhance. Not a damage dealer, a time-extender for sustain builds and burn builds (burn needs long fights).

Glimshade (SR, hybrid): Gold Sentinel Enhancement supports its direct skill output; Gold Healing Enhancement can support its heal. The healing effect depends on the target actually being burned, not merely having a burn drone equipped. Check that your chosen burn drone is applying burn reliably.

Doomblast (SSR, defensive): Gold Heal Enhancement and Gold Sentinel Enhancement are especially valuable together because the latter multiplies direct sentinel healing and the former applies through the Healing Enhance–Decrease multiplier. Purple Heal Enhancement and Heal Reduction can be useful supporting passives. Enemy Sentinel Decrease can reduce its heal, but a bonus does not make Doomblast immune to that counter.

Rendclaw (SSR, anti-heal): Heal Reduction and Sentinel Enhancement support its debuff and direct-damage roles. Avoid spending on Heal Enhancement solely for Rendclaw when its skill does not provide a direct heal. The exact second, third, and fourth passive priorities should reflect whether you need damage, extra anti-heal, or another counter.

content.html: Sentinel Enhancement increases sentinel damage and sentinel healing. Under the combat-mechanics paper’s model, it multiplies the sentinel’s direct output after its base skill coefficient is calculated; it does not automatically multiply separate fixed buffs that a sentinel grants, such as an elemental-enhancement rider. For example, a 440% direct-damage skill with +75% net Sentinel Enhancement would have a 770% effective direct coefficient before other factors. Enemy Sentinel Decrease changes the net bonus.

content.title: Recast Core and Protection Core Costs

content.html: Every sentinel recast uses 20 Recast Cores, regardless of how many slots are protected. Additional Protection Cores are consumed each time based on locked slots:

Protection Cores are scarce; event shops include Star Scramble, Hyper Battlefield, Planet Wars and Titan, plus some limited events. The first daily paid pack has been 15 Protection Cores for $3, but later packs can cost more. At $0.20/core, 1/2/3 locked slots add $4/$8/$20 of Protection Core material per recast, before Recast Cores. Prioritize scarce reroll materials for high-value SSR sentinels; consider purchasing additional affordable SR copies to hunt a desirable first passive.

content.title: Sentinel Choices by Build and Budget

content.html: Choose your main role first and build an affordable sentinel you can develop. Use the higher-rarity examples as longer-term options, not a requirement to follow the rarity ladder. Ticket income, Overclock Chips, and event availability determine how quickly you can progress; see the cost table for arithmetic.

cells: Stormquill or SavagePlate w/ gold crit damage
No essential SR; develop starter while saving for Rendclaw

Flashstrike (N-class), with useful damage-focused passives. One legion-recommended target is gold/purple/blue Crit Damage plus gold Sentinel Enhancement; check that those four slots are available before targeting the full combination.
Glimshade (hybrid; its healing needs the enemy to be burning, typically supplied by a burn drone)
(none essential, PVE scales well without an SSR)

content.html: Develop an affordable sentinel that is already useful to your main formation, then consider an SR or SSR when you have a clear reason to switch. Higher rarity does not automatically beat a more developed lower-rarity unit, but do not spend solely to complete a fixed starter → SR → SSR sequence. Compare the actual passive slots, skill, ticket costs, and battle role.

Gridstar (G-class): a strong defensive starter. Its timed heal works well with sustain-oriented PVP builds. A gold Heal Enhancement passive at level 10 adds +100 percentage points of Healing Enhancement; 40-star evolution supports passive levels up to 10. Ladybug’s triggered heal and other healing sources can benefit from Healing Enhancement, but the final amount depends on enemy Healing Decrease and the rest of the build. A developed Gridstar with a suitable passive can outperform an immature higher-rarity pick.

Stormquill (G-class): defensive-debuff alternative. Its talent reduces the opponent’s damage boost rather than granting a crit-specific bonus. It can still work with a Crit-focused chip formation, but choose it for the defensive debuff and compare it with Savageplate or other offensive options instead of treating it as intrinsically crit-oriented.

Flashstrike (N-class): a PVE option for Titan Challenge and Legion Hunt. Its timed damage-boost effect can amplify the damage your burning drones deal, not just the sentinel’s own attack. A legion-recommended passive goal is Crit Damage in gold, purple and blue, plus gold Sentinel Enhancement, where your developed sentinel has the necessary slots. This is a specialized player recommendation, not a confirmed mathematical optimum; test it against your existing sentinel using boss results.

Savageplate (N-class): fast offensive option. Its two-second skill cooldown makes it useful for short PVP fights and repeated direct hits. A Healing Decrease passive helps counter sustain-heavy opponents; compare that effect with your other damage sources rather than assuming it always wins. Rendclaw also has a two-second cycle, but its kit and cost are different.

Arcglow and Glimshade (SR): Arcglow is a sustain option for long PVP fights. Glimshade combines damage with healing that activates when the enemy is burning, so a burn drone is a practical way to trigger it. Its effect is conditional on the target’s status, not simply on equipping a burner.

SSR-class (e.g., Doomblast, Rendclaw): Strictly long-term investments. At its much higher acquisition cost, completing 40 copies is a long-term project. SSR copies from full Sentinel Event rounds can accelerate it. Combo bonuses can justify obtaining a separate SSR even before evolving it. Only SavagePlate and Rendclaw share the 2-second skill cooldown. Doomblast fires every 4 seconds but its healing enhancement (+10%) stacks up to 5 times, giving it strong long-fight value once maxed.

Preference: Skip R-class sentinels unless one fills a specific gap. I'd focus first on useful maxed G-class options, then build an SR for your main role. Treat any SSR as a long-term investment rather than a short-term upgrade.

Limited battle-log observations suggest that, when sentinels fire at the same time, the higher-BP player’s sentinel may act first. The supplied mechanics reference explicitly notes that more testing is needed; treat this as a possible timing factor, not a confirmed rule.

content.html: Doomblast’s +10% Healing Enhancement stack begins after each heal, so it boosts later heals. Flashstrike’s temporary boost may help burn stacks applied in that window, but that timing interaction has not been directly tested. Arcglow and Glimshade healing effects work in PVP, not PVE; their damage effects are separate. A strong general healing passive priority for Arcglow is gold and then purple Healing Enhancement.

Build a sentinel that supports the formation you use most. Once it performs reliably, consider a second sentinel for a distinct job, such as Healing Decrease, extra sustain, or direct damage. Check your current passive slots and event currency before spending on duplicate copies.

SR and SSR sentinels require far more acquisition resources. Their permanent combination bonuses can justify an unlock, but don’t delay a useful maxed starter to chase a rare sentinel. Preference: invest in a small roster of strong, usable sentinels before perfect rolls or endgame rarity.

Choose a sentinel you keep (with the desired passive) and a developed sentinel you sacrifice. The kept sentinel retains all its existing passive rolls; evolution stars from the sacrificed sentinel transfer to it. As new passive slots open during the merge, they roll randomly. All passive rolls on the sacrificed sentinel are lost.

Example: keep a one-star sentinel with a gold Healing Enhancement roll, then merge an older 40-star copy into it. The resulting evolved sentinel retains that gold roll and gains newly generated passives in the other slots. Level down the sacrificed sentinel first to reclaim Overclock Chips before merging.
This technique is especially useful for economical sentinels, such as Arcglow at 300 Sentinel Chips per copy, when searching for a valuable gold passive is cheaper than repeated locked recasts.

Every rarity requires 40 total sentinel copies to max evolution and passive progression. Copy acquisition costs differ dramatically by rarity, but the leveling and Overclock Chip progression mechanics are shared. For expensive SSR copies, plan around full Sentinel Event milestones and preferred-SSR refresh counters, not a fixed number of daily tickets. Level to 80 for maximum active skill; leveling beyond 80 toward 150 is optional raw-strength investment.

You can equip three mech spirits. In addition to the three active skills you choose, your collection provides permanent attribute bonuses and named combination bonuses. There are 14 documented combinations with up to 22 levels each; for example, Quantum Shift provides Dodge and can reach +44% once all required spirits reach level 60. Investing in mechs you do not equip can still help through collection stats and combinations, but prioritize accessible bonuses rather than buying indiscriminately.

Mech spirits follow a repeating 5-level cycle. At levels 1 through 4, you unlock or upgrade one attribute bonus slot each level (one slot at level 1, up to four at level 4). At level 5, the core skill upgrades. The cycle repeats: levels 6–9 upgrade attribute slots, level 10 upgrades the core skill again, and so on.

After addressing major pilot weaknesses, consider mech spirits as another valuable place to invest. Check the permanent stat lines and combination requirements for the spirits you already own, then invest where you can reach a useful bonus. Building every spirit equally is usually slower than targeting one clear upgrade or combination.

items.html: Aqua Spirit (SSR): broad PVP choice and especially powerful with healing. At skill level 1, the first drop below 30% HP grants +35% Final Damage Decrease for the entire remaining battle; at skill level 13, the trigger rises to 96% HP. The reduction persists after healing.

Berserk Dragon (SR): from +10% Final Damage Decrease at skill level 1 to +34% at level 13, active from the beginning for the full battle. Pairs with Aqua Spirit for defense but uses another mech slot.
Gloom Moon: situational Hit Rate counter against high Dodge.
Battle Diva: situational defense against high-Crit opponents.

Ladybug (N): first time HP falls below 30%, heal 6.25% maximum HP at skill level 1 or 21.25% at level 13. PVP only and once per battle. Healing Enhancement scales this heal, so it becomes very strong in heal builds. Ladybug cannot be obtained through selectable mech rewards: repeated Mech Event participation is the main way to level it.
Aqua Spirit + Berserk Dragon: persistent Final Damage Decrease; displayed bonuses should not be read as literal percent reduction in final incoming damage.

Toad Lord (SR): every 2 seconds, when a fighter/main gun/wing gun/missile attack crits, removes three Burn stacks from you and gains Crit Damage for the battle. At skill level 1, +7.5% per stack up to eight (+60%); at level 13, +25.5% per stack up to eight (+204%). Weak versus high-Crit-Resistance targets. Do not pair with Evil Eye: Blackout testing and discussion indicate Evil Eye converts away the normal weapon crits needed to trigger it.
Venom Scorpion: supports conventional weapon-Crit offense when you can still crit through enemy Crit Resistance.
Flame Stinger: situational finisher below its enemy-HP threshold.

Evil Eye (SR): converts eligible Crit Rate to Burn Crit Rate (10% → ~2% at skill level 1; 10% → 5.6% at level 13) and grants +25.5% Burn Damage Boost at max. PVE Burn centerpiece, not recommended for PVP Crit.

Star Envoy (SSR): requires three burn drones. Every third drone skill has a chance to add a stack of Burn Damage Boost, up to five stacks. The chance increases 10 percentage points per 10% Burn Enhancement over enemy Burn Decrease, up to 100%. Level 1 grants +25% boost per stack (up to +125%); level 13 grants +85% per stack (up to +425% additive stacks).
Dragon Emperor or another damage-bonus mech: consider once the core Burn/Crit mechanics are in place; compare actual boss damage.
Magic Armor: a bridge when extra Burn Enhancement is still needed to reach the cap.

content.title: How Evil Eye and Star Envoy Work Together

content.html: Evil Eye and Star Envoy do different jobs in PVE: Evil Eye creates Burn Crit Rate from eligible Crit Rate; Star Envoy builds Burn Damage Boost across repeated skills by a trio of burning drones. Both benefit from reaching 100% effective Burn Enhancement. Use Evil Eye in PVE, not in a conventional PVP Crit build with Toad Lord. Burn Crit Rate caps at 80%; against a target with zero Crit Resistance, max Evil Eye needs approximately 142.9% Crit Rate to reach it.

You equip one engine for a battle. Different engines contribute Hit Rate, Crit Resistance, or elemental Decrease, with values depending on the engine’s current grade and whether it is equipped. Read the shared and equipped bonuses on the engine screen before calculating the benefit; do not assume every grade simply doubles a passive percentage.
Hit Rate is the offensive choice; Crit Resistance and elemental Decrease engines defend against particular threats. Pick the engine for the matchup, not simply the highest-level one.

cells: Punch through opponent dodge on offense; general-purpose pick when you don't know the matchup
Deny crits against a high-crit, low-dodge opponent. Also my go-to defensive engine in Star Scramble.
Counter burn-heavy opponents (critical defensive layer for dodge/heal builds)

content.html: Hit Rate and Crit Resistance are the two you'll use most. The elemental decrease engines are situational, worth leveling over time but lower priority unless you're seeing a specific damage type.
Three defaults cover most situations:

items.html: General offense: Hit Rate. It's what makes the rest of your investments pay off against high-dodge opponents.
Star Scramble defense: Crit Resistance. Fights span multiple attack attempts, heal/dodge carries you through, and the big-damage spikes come from crits.
Facing a known damage type: the matching Decrease engine (Burn Decrease, Electric Decrease, Reflect Decrease).

content.html: Camp Technology contains Basic, Advanced, and Top upgrades; Super Technology is a separate research track reached through the Camp area. These are distinct from Legion Technology. Invest according to the stats you actually use, the current unlocks, and the cost of the next level rather than treating all Camp upgrades as interchangeable.

Camp upgrades generally become more expensive as you progress, and different camps have different cost curves. Some upgrades add BP without materially improving the fights you care about. Weigh their real impact against matchmaking and opportunity cost; a higher BP is not by itself evidence that the upgrade was worthwhile.

For PVP, compare Final Damage Increase/Decrease first, then PVP damage and reduction, and then your build’s specific gaps. This is a practical priority framework, not a universal purchase sequence. If an upgrade is locked or very expensive, spend where the next attainable level helps your actual matchups.

items.html: Final Damage Increase (FDI) and Final Damage Decrease (FDD). The net final-damage value is 100 + your FDI − opponent FDD. At a net value of 50, the damage multiplier is 0.50×; at 40, it is about 0.417×. The formula actually softens further reductions below 50—there is no sudden cliff. FDI and FDD still matter greatly, particularly FDD against strong opponents; Crystal Prism and Eternal Pivot are early FDD options in Super Technology; Source Essence provides another FDD path if you have unlocked it.
PVP Damage and PVP Damage Reduction. Core PVP scaling after FDI/FDD stabilize.
Burn Enhancement (Top Tech). Adds to the sources that can get a PVE build to 100% raw Burn Enhancement without dedicating chip slots to Burn.

Hit Rate, Crit Resistance, Dodge, Crit Rate (Top Technology). Raise the stats that address real matchup gaps; level 10 can be a review point, not a required stop or a fixed rotation. Round out the stat profile after the big three above are in place.

content.html: Basic Camp Technology provides Maingun, Winggun, Missile Attack, and HP upgrades across individual camps. Buy inexpensive upgrades with real value to the equipment you use; early camps can be less costly than later ones. Compare Attack and HP needs rather than assuming a single fixed order is optimal for every fighter.

Inside Camp → Super Technology, SkyEagle Tech provides Final Damage Increase. Crystal Prism Tech and Eternal Pivot Tech provide Final Damage Decrease; Source Essence Tech is another FDD source when unlocked. One legion recommendation was to take the first three named options toward level 80 and other accessible Super Technologies toward level 60. That is a player’s investment plan, not a mandatory sequence, and availability and costs can change.

Choose a Titan gear set that matches your fighter and the content you play. Completing a matching five-piece Titan setup increases adjusted weapon attack in the combat-mechanics model, which also feeds drone, sentinel, and mech damage. Do not confuse the fighter with the equipment set needed to qualify for a bonus.

items.html: Conqueror (physical). Pair the Conqueror fighter with matching Titan equipment to obtain the appropriate set bonuses. The fighter name and the gear-set name refer to different items.
Destroyer (energy). A common choice for energy builds. Titan Challenge modifiers can change how different sets perform, so check the active season and your actual damage before committing shards.

Thor (energy). An alternative energy set, often lower priority than Destroyer for a dedicated Destroyer build. Certain Titan seasons may reward particular Thor pieces; compare the active season and your owned pieces before spending shards.

content.html: The combat-mechanics paper models a 1.3× adjusted-attack factor for a complete five-piece Titan setup. Since drones, sentinels, and mechs scale with that adjusted attack, breaking the set can cost more than the swapped equipment appears to gain. This is a reason to compare complete sets, not proof that every mixed-gear setup always loses; test a change against the mode you play.

Keep the gear needed for your active Titan set before reclaiming surplus pieces. Avoid downgrading or using spare pieces as upgrade material without checking the resulting attribute loss and resource return. Non-Titan equipment is not all interchangeable; compare actual stats and effects instead of assuming every normal piece performs the same.

If you do not yet have the matching Titan winggun, Prism Winggun is a reasonable interim PVE choice. A legion member recommends using it until you obtain Destroyer Winggun; this is a practical option, not a universal best-in-slot rule.

Legion Technology upgrades weapon/armor stats and bonuses against specific enemy categories. In the game it is divided into Equipment Reinforce, Damage Increase, and Enemy Weakened. It uses Legion Points and Stars. This is separate from Camp Technology and Super Technology.

Prioritize the two aerial-specific lines for PVP. In Legion Technology → Damage Increase, the upgrade is “Increase damage against aerial enemies (including players).” The defensive counterpart is in Legion Technology → Enemy Weakened: “Reduce damage from aerial enemies (including players).” These affect fights with other players and the maximum listed level is 100 for each. The offensive aerial bonus is useful across multiple damage sources, so it often offers broader value than a single-weapon upgrade. These are long-term priorities, not requirements to max both before upgrading anything else.

In Legion Technology → Equipment Reinforce, each weapon has upgrades to Base Attack, Attack Rate, Crit Rate and Crit Damage. For a Destroyer energy PVP build, here is a practical way to decide which to raise next:

items.html: Start with the weapon dealing meaningful damage. Compare current Maingun, Winggun and Missile stats rather than assuming the same order for every build.
Base Attack is broadly useful when that weapon contributes significant damage. Crit Rate matters when you still have effective crit headroom, and Crit Damage is stronger when crits happen often.
Attack Rate increases the number of attacks, so it can be competitive with raw damage upgrades. Compare costs and current rates; it does not belong permanently at the bottom of a universal ranking.

content.html: There is no demonstrated universal sequence of Base Attack → Crit Rate → Crit Damage → Attack Rate. In the mechanics reference, rainbow Titan Winggun has a base cooldown of about 1.6 seconds and damage coefficient of 0.09; Missile has about 4 seconds and 0.225, respectively. Those factors approximately offset before individual weapon attack values, attack-speed upgrades, crit effects and other bonuses. The right next level depends on your current build and its cost.

Keep Armor Base HP competitive. If you are losing because you cannot survive, improve HP rather than completing every weapon upgrade first. Players focused on PVP can put Ground/Sea, Boss, Normal Enemy, and Strong Foe bonuses lower on the list; keep those if Titan Challenge or Legion Hunt damage matters to you. Before resetting Legion Technology, check what you would lose in PVE.

Military Rank is separate from Legion Technology and Camp research. It offers account-wide progression and combat attributes; evaluate the specific Attack/HP gains you can afford rather than treating rank upgrades as a substitute for build-specific stats.
Build strategy is half the game. The other half is accumulating resources so when the right event lands you have the stockpile to use.

This is a suggested daily spending plan, not a minimum required to compete. If your diamond income is lower, prioritize the upgrades that address your biggest weakness rather than trying to fund every system at once. The figures below describe a full routine, not a rule for every player.

items.html: Engine parts: 140💎. Direct contribution to a stat you equip every battle.

Three daily challenge resources (AirSea Simulation, Critical Strike, Sentinel Base): an example routine budgets 100 diamonds each, 300 total. Choose which to refresh based on your actual pilot, drone, and sentinel needs; this is not a mandatory daily charge.
Chip factory parts: 100💎. Faster chip production compounds over months.

Optional daily-shop purchases: Older legion examples include R pilot chests around 60 diamonds, Alloy around 60, and discounts on Rhenite or Recruitment Tickets. Verify current prices and buy only if those materials are part of your plan.

content.html: The full plan totals about 540💎 per day before optional shop purchases. Spending less means slower progress in some systems, not that your build stops being competitive. Pick the parts that matter most to you.

Save event-specific currencies because milestone progress resets for each new event. Within an event, several events permit up to four reward rounds. The weekly theme schedule and current reward values can change, so confirm the live milestone screen before committing.

content.html: Drone Event milestones count 8,000 Rhenite of qualifying spend per round; up to four rounds are available and the progress resets at each event. Purchased drones can be resold for 80% of their purchase price, but their full purchase price counts toward the milestone. Without refreshes, an 8,000-spend round therefore costs a theoretical net 1,600 Rhenite.

Refreshing the shop costs 10 Rhenite and counts toward progress but cannot be refunded. If a round spends 8,000 total including refreshes, approximate net spend is 1,600 + 80% of refresh costs; overshooting the threshold adds some expense. A documented example with 26 refreshes and 7,800 in drone purchases totals 8,060 milestone spend and 1,820 net cost after 80% refunds.

Drone recasts spend Modified Chips that count at 2× their quantity toward Drone Event progress; those chips are consumed rather than refunded. Save meaningful recasts for the event. The exact cost of a round depends on purchases, refreshes, and recasts. Use the Drone Event Calculator to model your inventory. Players with a Volley Vortex pass may find all four rounds easier; without it, two or three rounds are achievable for some active players.

The Pilot Event requires 300 pulls per full reward round and permits up to four rounds; progress resets between events. Save tickets so you can finish a round rather than spending into incomplete milestones. Many active players can manage one round and occasionally two with diamonds. SR pilot selectables from the event can target the equipped pilots you intend to awaken.

A full Sentinel Event reward round requires 8,000 Sentinel Chips spent. Milestone progress resets each event and can repeat up to four rounds (32,000 spent). Skipping an event to save for a full round is usually better than spending partway toward an expiring milestone. Completing a round grants a selectable SSR in addition to SSR copies bought during the round.

Shop refreshes: four free daily refreshes, or paid refreshes costing 10 Sentinel Chips each; both count toward the SSR refresh counters. One SSR is guaranteed every 20 refreshes, and bonus random SSR appearances do not reset that counter. These refresh counters persist between events.

Pick a preferred SSR. After five appearances of a nonpreferred SSR (you do not need to buy them), the next refresh guarantees your preferred SSR. This counter carries between events, and changing preferred selection does not reset it. An appearance of the preferred SSR resets the counter whether purchased or not.

You can use free refreshes before the next event to leave a preferred SSR on the shop screen, then stop refreshing until the event starts so the purchase counts toward the new milestone. Each SSR costs 1,000 chips, with one copy per appearance. A full round may yield roughly four to five preferred copies from refreshes plus the selectable milestone reward, depending on luck and spending. Extra low-rarity sentinel purchases can fill remaining milestone spend, but manage inventory slots (additional slots have cost 500 diamonds).

A 40-copy SSR is a long-term goal, not a quick upgrade. Collecting all required sentinels for a combo bonus activates it manually; do not assume its persistence after selling a component without testing.
